native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: The summed social-capital Z-score peaks in the Late Únětice / Old Bronze Age (OBA), at SocCap = +4.238082, achieved in both BCE 1400 and BCE 1300 (a tied 200-year plateau). The chronologically earlier — and therefore canonical first-occurrence — peak century is BCE 1400. The components that rise into the peak are Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU) and Monument Count (ZMonument): from BCE 1500 to BCE 1400 CopperGold moves from −0.36 to +2.54 Z (+2.90 Z) and MonumentCount moves from +0.165 to +1.708 Z (+1.543 Z), together producing essentially the entire +4.58 Z sum-increase into the peak; both are also far above the long BCE 3200–1700 baseline (CopperGold +2.93 Z, MonumentCount +1.45 Z). Amber (Zamber) increases only marginally into and around the peak (+0.14 Z into it, +0.13 Z vs. baseline) and is not the driver. The peak is a co-occurrence of very high Copper/Gold and very high Monument-Count signals in the OBA horizon, robust to using raw anchor values or block-mean of *_inter (sensitivity peak also BCE 1400 with SocCap = 4.238082)."
native_result.WorkflowB: Load data/capital.csv (39 rows, BCE 4300..500 in 100-yr steps; decimal separator is comma) and data/time_series_data.csv (3601 rows, CE −4100..−500). Drop metadata columns (group, color). For each of the 39 century rows compute SocCap = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument. Locate the maximum (4.238082) and identify ties — both BCE 1400 and BCE 1300 carry identical component values (2.54, −0.01, 1.708082). Adopt BCE 1400 as the chronologically earliest (= largest BCE) canonical occurrence. For each component, compute Δ entering the peak from the immediately preceding century (BCE 1500→1400) and Δ vs. the long MN/SG/LN baseline at BCE 3200..1700 (n=16). Cross-check by grouping time_series_data.csv into 100-yr windows and block-averaging the *_inter series (sensitivity); peak location (BCE 1400) and value (4.238082) are unchanged."

sub_hypo.text: Copper & Gold and Monument Count jointly drive essentially the entire social-capital increase into the peak, while Amber contributes only marginally.
sub_hypo.context: Transition from BCE 1500 to BCE 1400, entering the Late Únětice / Old Bronze Age social-capital peak.

sub_hypo.text: The peak co-occurs with Copper & Gold and Monument Count far above the long baseline, whereas Amber is only slightly above baseline and is not the driver.
sub_hypo.context: BCE 1400 peak compared with the BCE 3200–1700 MN/SG/LN baseline of 16 century observations.

sub_hypo.text: The canonical social-capital peak is robust to using raw anchor values or 100-year block means of interpolated component series.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity comparison of century-level capital data with time-series data spanning CE −4100 to −500, grouped into 100-year windows.
sub_hypo.relations: Summing raw component anchors and summing 100-year block-averaged interpolated components both yield the canonical peak at BCE 1400 with SocCap = 4.238082.
